analysis.title: Situation Room: Midterms IG impact: neutral
key_insights: BofA sees the election impact on the IG credit outlook as mostly neutral. A split government and gridlock were mostly priced in. The surprise was a larger Democratic win in Congress and in gubernatorial races.

Risk assets rallied after the Democratic sweep in the Midterm elections, mostly because oil fell. Brent (2nd contract) fell 8% on the day and 18% so far in November, with no escalation in hostilities after the elections.
BofA continues to prefer hedging Iran risks because there is no apparent progress toward a deal.

The most consequential market and economic implication of the Blue Sweep, per BofA economists, is tighter AI regulation at the state and local level. That triggered concerns about slower US growth and some bull steepening in the Treasury curve.
Tighter AI regulation could make the AI data center buildout more expensive. BofA considers it unlikely to significantly derail AI deployment or IG market AI funding needs in 2027.

Consensus 2027 capex for AMZN, GOOGL and META was revised higher again after 3Q earnings, to $854bn, while free cash flow after dividends was revised lower. The revision was smaller than in prior quarters, which BofA reads as improving clarity.
Consensus 2027 FCF less dividends for AMZN, GOOGL and META is now -$160bn, versus -$95bn after 2Q earnings. This was the smallest revision in 12 months.
Consensus expects FCF less dividends for the three hyperscalers to improve to -$45bn in 2028 and turn positive in 2029. That implies the biggest funding need is in 2027.
ORCL has spelled out its funding needs through 2028 and MSFT is expected to stay FCF-positive, so BofA focuses on AMZN, GOOGL and META.

US IG issuance was $10bn across 5 deals on 11/4, $52.9bn week-to-date and month-to-date. The average new issue concession was 6.7bps, and this week's new issues trade 3bps tighter on average from pricing.

META priced a multi-tranche USD bond on 11/3 (5, 7, 10, 20 and 30 year, about $15bn total), with new issue concessions of 5 to 32bps. ORCL priced $10bn across 5 to 20 year tranches on 11/2 at spreads of 240 to 335bps.
Estimated IG dealer inventories of US issuer bonds rose to $7.4bn on 11/4 from -$7.8bn on 10/21. Estimated inventory DV01 rose to -$1.7mn from -$12.1mn.
Dealers added an estimated $2,002mn of IG inventory on 11/4, $14,088mn over the past week and $25,161mn over 4 weeks. Banks/Brokers (+$387mn) and Energy (+$384mn) led the daily change.
Daily HG fund flow was -$1,270mn on 11/3, down from +$4,671mn on 11/2. Average daily HG inflow was $364mn in November versus $708mn in October.
HG fund flows have tended to follow returns since Oct-2023 but have been decoupled from returns since about Oct-2024.

Foreign demand proxies on 11/4: net dealer volume before 8am was -$146mn for 1-10yr bonds and +$177mn for 10yr+ bonds. Dealer-to-affiliate volume from 8am to noon was -$40mn for 1-10yr and +$62mn for 10yr+.
